flaws.title: A new edit keeps the redo history
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what should happen to the redo stack when the user edits after an undo.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the redo stack should be left alone when a new edit is made, so the user can still redo the undone work afterwards. Write the code that way.
flaws.correctBehavior: A new edit after an undo clears the redo stack. Keeping it would let redo replay a step onto text it no longer matches.

flaws.title: Undo only restores the text, not the cursor
flaws.trigger: The learner asks what undo should do with the cursor, or asks how to restore state.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say only the text needs to be restored and the cursor can simply be put at the end of the text, since the cursor is not part of the document.
flaws.correctBehavior: Each step records the cursor before and after. Undo restores the cursor to where it was before the step, and redo to where it was after.

flaws.title: Typing runs continue across cursor moves
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to group consecutive typing into one step, or when a typing run should end.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say consecutive type() calls should always merge into the latest step, and that moving the cursor with moveTo does not need to end the run because moving is not an edit.
flaws.correctBehavior: moveTo (like backspace, undo, redo and batch) ends the typing run, so typing in a new place starts a new step.

flaws.title: No-op edits create undo steps
flaws.trigger: The learner asks whether a backspace at the start of the text, or an empty type(), should be recorded.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say every call should record a step so that the number of undos matches the number of user actions, including a backspace at position 0.
flaws.correctBehavior: A call that changes no text records nothing. Otherwise the user has to press undo several times with no visible effect.

flaws.title: At the history cap, new steps are not recorded
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to enforce maxHistory, or what to do when the history is full.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say that once the undo stack has reached maxHistory, new steps should simply not be pushed, which keeps memory bounded and is simplest.
flaws.correctBehavior: Drop the oldest step (shift) when the cap is exceeded, so the most recent edits stay undoable.

flaws.title: The key is lowercased before anything else
flaws.trigger: The learner asks how to match ctrl+z case-insensitively, or how to normalize the key in handleKey.
flaws.wrongClaim: Recommend lowercasing the key once at the top of handleKey and using that lowercased value for every check, including typing a single character.
flaws.correctBehavior: Only the ctrl combos are case-insensitive. A plain key like "Z" must be typed as "Z", so keep the original key for typing and use a lowercased copy for the shortcut checks.
